_comment: Committed PDK + tool defaults for the layout evidence under layout/.
This is the layout-verification sibling of sim/pdk.json -- deliberately
a SEPARATE file, per sim/pdk.json's own precedent (this repo has no
design/pdk.json; the schematic/netlist flow doesn't need a PDK install,
only xschem's own sky130 symbol library). open_pdks_commit below
matches sim/pdk.json's exactly -- both pin the same open_pdks release,
verified 2026-09-15.
variant           sky130 flavor directory used to generate/verify
every layout/ evidence directory below
open_pdks_commit  provenance pin, matches sim/pdk.json
klt_deck          the klayout-tools (`klt`) curated rule-deck name
resolved for this PDK family (--deck sky130 on
every klt drc / klt extract / klt lvs invocation
under layout/). klt's curated decks are built in --
no real open_pdks install is required to run the
layout/ chain itself, only to resolve --pdk sky130A
for `klt gen`'s own PDK-family role-layer tables.
klt_version_pin   the klt build this evidence was last generated/
verified against, from `klt version --format json`'s
`version` field. A provenance pin, not a hard gate --
re-verifying with a different klt build is expected
to happen and should update this pin plus the
affected evidence directories together, mirroring
2AMLogic/sky130-trng's layout/pdk.json precedent
(this recipe's own reference, see layout/README.md).
klt_commit_pin    the SAME build as klt_version_pin, spelled as the
unambiguous git_commit `klt version --format json`
reports (matched by prefix: this is the short
abbreviated form already embedded after the `+g` in
klt_version_pin above, e.g. `0.4.0+gba213c617b4e` ->
`ba213c617b4e`). THIS field, not klt_version_pin's
leading semver, is what actually identifies the
build: the same commit can be packaged under more
than one semver (a local `+g<hash>` build bumps
package_version independently of git_commit), and
the converse has also been observed in a churning
toolchain -- see layout/README.md. layout/bin/
_klt_common.py's check_klt_pin() compares the
installed klt's git_commit against this field once
per compose-cell.py run and WARNS (never hard-fails)
on a mismatch, so a stale install self-reports
instead of surfacing deep in the chain as a
confusing 'unrecognized key(s)' error (issue #51).
